laws.heading: Embu County: no alcohol for under 18s
laws.rule: Embu County Alcoholic Drinks Control Act, 2021, s 29: no person may sell, supply or provide an alcoholic drink to a person under 18. The penalty is a fine of up to KES 150,000 (about A$1,639; A$1 = KES 91.49 (CBK rate KES 129.96 per USD, 29 Oct 2026, with RBA A$1 = USD 0.7040, 30 Oct 2026)) or up to 1 year in prison, or both. A seller has a defence if they asked to see an age document and believed on reasonable grounds that it was genuine. The Act also bars under-18s from the part of licensed premises where alcohol is made, stored, sold or consumed.
laws.penalty_signal: Up to KES 150,000 (about A$1,639) or 1 year for the seller

laws.heading: Embu County: where and when alcohol can be sold or drunk
laws.rule: Embu County Alcoholic Drinks Control Act, 2021, s 35 (breach of licence): except as the Act provides, no person may sell alcohol in a workplace, office, factory, public park, public recreational facility, public transport vehicle, public beach, sports stadium or public street, and no person may sell, buy or drink alcohol at a selling outlet after the hours for which the outlet is licensed. For selling without the right licence, a first offence carries a fine of up to KES 50,000 (about A$546) or up to 9 months in prison; a second offence up to KES 100,000 (about A$1,093) or 1 year. Licence hours are in the First Schedule (s 13(3)): for a general retail on-licence, Monday to Friday 4.00 pm to 11.00 pm; for a general off-licence selling wines and spirits, 2.00 pm to 8.30 pm; for a supermarket off-licence, 10.00 am to 8.30 pm. A hotel may sell to lodgers at any hour. Weekend hours in the schedule text were not legible and are not stated here.
laws.penalty_signal: Fines and imprisonment under the county Act
